title: Implement a functional interface with one lambda per operator

blocks.text: A functional interface has exactly one abstract method; it may also carry default and static methods. A lambda supplies the body of that one abstract method, and the compiler uses its signature to type the lambda.
The interface `Calculator` is given, in the same file: its single abstract method is `int calculate(int a, int b)`, with a default `square(int n)` and a static `add(int a, int b)`.

Write `Calculators.of(char operator)`, which returns a `Calculator` lambda for `'+'`, `'-'`, `'*'` or `'/'` (integer division). Any other operator throws `IllegalArgumentException` with the message `unknown operator: <operator>`, for example `unknown operator: %`.
Consider *when* a bad operator should be reported, and what dividing by zero must do.

cases.says: Each of + - * / gives a Calculator that computes that operation.
A lambda-made Calculator still has the interface's default method.
An unknown operator is rejected when of() is called, not later when the calculator runs.
Dividing by zero throws ArithmeticException instead of returning a made-up number.

concepts: A lambda can only implement a functional interface: one abstract method, with any number of default or static methods.
